title: India Inc Festive Revenue Holds Up as Margins Shrink in Q2
excerpt: ICRA expects Q2 revenue growth of 13-15% on festive stocking, but operating margins to contract 100-150 basis points, while Mint consensus sees Nifty EBITDA falling 9.3% despite 18.6% revenue growth.
body:
• ICRA projects India Inc revenue growth of 13-15% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, down from 21.3% in Q1, supported by domestic consumption and festive-season stocking.
  • The twist is profit: ICRA expects operating margins to contract 100-150 basis points year-on-year on higher raw material, fuel, freight and packaging costs.
  • Mint calculations from Bloomberg consensus put the split starkly for Nifty companies excluding financials: revenue up 18.6% year-on-year, but EBITDA down 9.3% year-on-year and 14.5% sequentially.
  • For investors, the quarter rewards domestic-demand names — autos, retail, consumer durables and hospitality — over export-linked IT, apparel and diamonds, and penalises names that cannot pass costs through.

India's listed companies are heading into a festive quarter that lifts sales and squeezes profit at the same time. Rating agency ICRA projects revenue growth of 13-15% year-on-year in the July-September quarter of 2026-27, down from 21.3% in the June quarter, with domestic consumption, festive-season trade stocking and favourable commodity realisations supporting the topline, according to The Hindu BusinessLine reporting on ICRA's analysis of 2,756 listed non-financial companies.

The bottom line tells a different story. ICRA warned that operating profit margins could contract by 100-150 basis points year-on-year in Q2, pressured by elevated raw material, fuel, freight and packaging costs that have risen largely due to the ongoing West Asia conflict and the depreciation of the rupee against the dollar.

The Revenue-Profit Split, Quantified

The divergence is sharpest in consensus estimates for large companies. Mint calculations based on Bloomberg consensus, reported by Hellenic Shipping News from Livemint, showed 41 out of 50 Nifty companies excluding financials may post average revenue growth of 18.6% year-on-year in the September quarter. Over the same period, consensus earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation may decline 9.3% year-on-year and 14.5% sequentially.

Elara Securities said ex-financials EBITDA and overall Nifty net profits are expected to remain flat year-on-year owing to margin pressure. Ambit Asset Management said Nifty 50 earnings growth is expected to be muted at low single digits in Q2, due to margin compression in cyclicals and a high base.

Yes Securities put the duration on the squeeze: Q2 will mark five consecutive quarters of contraction in operating margins year-on-year for its coverage universe excluding financials and oil marketing companies. The same analysts said margins are likely to be flat sequentially, indicating signs of bottoming out in EBITDA margins. Even though crude oil and commodities have fallen from their June peaks, high-cost raw material inventory may continue to hurt companies before easing in Q3, the Mint report added.

"The corporate earnings cycle in Q2 2026-27 is likely to witness a divergence between healthy revenue growth and constrained operating profit margins, as seen in Q1 FY27."

— Jitin Makkar, Group Head for Corporate Ratings, ICRA

Who Gains, Who Gets Squeezed

ICRA expects sectors dependent on domestic demand — automobiles, retail, consumer durables and hospitality — to outperform export-oriented industries such as information technology, apparel and cut-and-polished diamonds, which face weak global demand and rising trade protectionism. Pent-up demand and stocking ahead of the festive season may help automobiles and consumer durables in particular, brokerages cited by Mint said, with revenue growth led by domestic-oriented sectors and consumption plays, led by financials and supported by consumer discretionaries.

On margins, oil refiners, aviation, FMCG and cement companies face the sharpest pressure, ICRA said. Metals, mining, telecom and select utilities are better positioned due to favourable realisations or cost pass-through mechanisms. Several companies have raised prices to pass on cost increases, ICRA noted, which is likely to dampen volume growth even as value-led growth continues — festive sales by value can therefore look stronger than festive sales by volume.

ICRA also flagged a downside risk from below-normal rainfall in August-September, which could weaken rural demand, push up food inflation and weigh on agri-linked and rural-focused sectors. Its group head Jitin Makkar said in Outlook Business reporting: "Persistent weakness in the global demand environment is likely to affect the performance of export-oriented sectors, while domestic demand remains relatively resilient."

Credit Still Holds, For Now

ICRA expects interest coverage to remain resilient at 4.9-5.2 times in Q2, broadly in line with 5.1 times in Q1. The quarter is therefore a profit problem, not a solvency problem: companies earn less per rupee of sales, not a failure to service debt.

What to Watch Next

The test for Q3 is pass-through and inventory. If high-cost inventory clears, the flat sequential margin signal could turn into recovery. If price hikes choke festive volume, revenue will slow while margins stay compressed. Watch gross margins in autos, FMCG and cement — the sectors ICRA named as most exposed — against headline revenue growth.
